rationale: DEPTH CAMPAIGN (2026-10-19, task-17): the receiver-IDENTITY evidence classes beyond the 2026-10-18 contract's field/param/local/return. Each is evidence the FILE states itself, so each is red-able with a flat fixture (no project index): `this` = an implicit-`this` call (JLS 15.12.1) and an explicit `this.m()`, where the enclosing type is the instance receiver; `super` = the first IN-FILE base that declares the method; `enum` = an enum-constant receiver, whose static type IS the enum (JLS 8.9.1) — pinned on CALLS and on a READ of the constant; `initializer` = `var` whose initializer states the type (JLS 14.4), both `new` and a single-return-type in-file method. THE NEGATIVES PIN THE GUARD: an unqualified call to a STATICALLY IMPORTED method is NOT an implicit-this member (JLS 7.5.3/7.5.4 — the enclosing type would be the wrong owner), and a member of an ENCLOSING class is not the inner class's own member (the receiver resolver only walks the enclosing chain, never outwards). A class-qualified static call (`Helper.help()`) stays owner-less — that refusal is pinned by java/receiver-owner-type's forbid, untouched here. THE SECOND WAVE adds the receiver-IDENTITY classes whose type is WRITTEN in the receiver expression itself: `new` (`new Widget().paint()`), `cast` (`((Widget) unknown).paint()`), and `element` (`widgets[0].paint()` — the array binding's declared element type). The last negative pins the guard: a receiver created as a LIBRARY type (`new StringBuilder().append(...)`) gets NO owner, because the channel would decline an owner the project does not declare.
